item.title: Inside Der Riese: The SS’s Most Guarded Underground Complex
item.author: Timeline - World History Documentaries
item.content:encoded:
A sealed valley. A stone “henge” test rig. Cables built to power a small city. What exactly were the Nazis building beneath the Owl Mountains?
Join Forbidden History as we descend into Der Riese — the SS’s most guarded underground complex — to investigate claims of a radical propulsion device codenamed Die Glocke. Guided by researcher Igor Witkowski, we explore flooded tunnels and intact blast doors, examine eerie remnants from SS weapon stores, and stand at a circular rig believed to test vertical liftoff craft. Along the way, we trace wartime Foo Fighter reports, the scramble for German scientists in Operation Paperclip, and the postwar Avrocar and Tarielka disc projects. Newly surfaced documents, prisoner testimonies, and deathbed confessions hint at an undertaking labeled “decisive for the war” — but what was really being tested here, and why did no forced laborers leave alive?
From stealth experiments to talk of anti-gravity, this investigation pieces together the most secret aviation research of the Third Reich without jumping to easy answers. Watch to see what the evidence reveals — and what still hides behind collapsed rock and classified files.

item.title: Private jets - How the richest travel | DW Documentary
item.author: DW Documentary
item.content:encoded:
Private jets: Symbols of luxury and exclusivity - but their high CO₂ emissions also make them increasingly controversial. This documentary explores the billion-dollar industry behind the aircraft of the ultra-rich.
Aircraft broker Ziporah presents one of the private jets she has for sale. With around 84 square meters of living space and two bedrooms, the plane looks more like a luxury apartment than a form of transportation. The purchase price: $25 million. Annual operating costs add about $5 million, while a single refueling can cost up to $40,000. Kolin is an entrepreneur who's developed a business model renting out private jets when their owners aren't using them. Booking is almost as easy as ordering a taxi - though the service is obviously much more exclusive. Travelers no longer even have to be millionaires to fly privately. So-called "empty-leg flights" - flights between two charter bookings without passengers - often offer last-minute seats at significantly reduced prices. But as the effects of climate change become increasingly visible, the industry faces mounting pressure. Many celebrities avoid making public appearances with their private jets to avoid attracting environmental activists' attention. Critics see the aircraft as symbols of excessive resource consumption in an era of global warming. The high emissions from flight activity of public figures like Taylor Swift, Elon Musk and Bernard Arnault have been publicly tracked - and heavily criticized. This documentary offers a fascinating look into the world of private aviation while asking whether mile-high luxury still has a place in our time.

item.title: Domestic violence and psychological terror | DW Documentary
item.author: DW Documentary
item.content:encoded:
Domestic violence often goes hand-in-hand with psychological and emotional abuse. This documentary examines those mechanisms through the lens of what's known as "coercive control."
The term describes the many forms of everyday abuse of power and control that perpetrators use to systematically dominate the people they harm. Their methods range from constant surveillance and intimidation to threats of murder.
Excessive jealousy, isolation, humiliation, insults, GPS tracking, cyberbullying, financial dependence and threats of suicide or murder are typical forms of coercive control and central elements of domestic violence. Understanding this pattern changes the way a situation can be viewed. Instead of asking, "Why doesn't she just leave him?” the crucial question becomes, "What is he doing to prevent her from leaving?”
This documentary sets out to explore that. It looks at how abusive partners describe and justify their actions and how lawmakers and the justice system assess such behaviors. Among those interviewed are judges specialized in the area - like Gwenola Joly-Coz, First President of the Court of Appeal of Poitiers, and Ombeline Mahuzier, President of the Colmar Judicial Court.
Coercive control was first recognized explicitly as a mechanism of domestic violence in a 2023 French court case. This documentary traces the dynamics and stages of escalation in this complex system of abuse, which seeks to make women dependent through psychological violence and deprive them of basic freedoms. In the worst cases, that domestic terror ends in femicide.
Special structures have been established at courts that handle domestic violence cases in Poitiers, Colmar and Paris. With special permission, court proceedings there were filmed. Perpetrators gave their own accounts of events. Their statements are contrasted with assessments by judges, offering a rare insight into the mechanisms of domestic violence.

ABSTRACT Many organizations still treat observability as a tooling decision: select a vendor, deploy agents, and expect insight to follow. Yet teams continue to struggle with fragmented signals, rising complexity, and slow incident response. The real issue is rarely the tool itself - it’s the absence of a shared foundation and a coherent product experience.
This talk reframes observability as an internal platform product, designed with clear users, sane defaults, and long-term evolution in mind. Drawing parallels to Kubernetes and platform engineering, we’ll explore why powerful primitives are not enough - and why standardization, correlation, and paved paths matter more than features.
We’ll look at how OpenTelemetry provides a vendor-neutral foundation for structured telemetry, decoupling instrumentation from backends and enabling correlation by default. This structured approach not only reduces cognitive load and improves reliability, it also lays the groundwork for AI-assisted debugging and natural language interaction with production systems.
Observability isn’t just about collecting more data. It’s about designing a platform that makes understanding systems easier - for both humans and machines.

item.title: The paradox of Latino ICE agents
item.author: Vox
item.content:encoded:
Under the second Trump administration, immigration enforcement agencies have undergone a significant expansion. President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill raised ICE’s budget from $10 billion to $85 billion, making it the most funded law enforcement agency in the United States. With that funding, they began offering economic incentives like signing bonuses and student loan forgiveness programs. The number of ICE agents and officers doubled in just one year, with another recruiting push underway through the end of 2026.
Today, perhaps more than ever, the front lines of those federal immigration law enforcement agencies reflect the demographics of the populations they were created to police. Latinos are overrepresented in the Department of Homeland Security, which houses ICE and Border Patrol. Self-identified Latinos account for nearly half of Border Patrol agents and about 30 percent of ICE agents.
So why do so many Latinos join the immigration enforcement agencies that have targeted their own communities? The answers reveal complexities about American Latino identity and the splintered points of view on immigration policy at the border.
Hosted by Kahlil Greene, this video is part of our new series, Kahlil Explains, that unites Vox’s unique brand of explainer journalism with Greene’s expertise in how politics and culture shape society. This episode traces the evolution of immigration enforcement agencies and their appeal to Latino recruits, to explain why so many ICE and Border Patrol agents are Latino.

item.title: Space power struggle: Is a new space race looming? | DW Documentary
item.author: DW Documentary
item.content:encoded:
Space services have grown essential to our everyday lives: GPS, satellite internet and communications from orbit. Beyond civilian use, space systems are driving military conflict, fuelling a race for dominance in space.
The United States is planning a new missile defence system known as the 'Golden Dome.' In September 2026, it officially confirmed for the first time that it had already deployed weapons in orbit. China is rapidly expanding its own space program, working toward its own space ecosystem, including a lunar base. India, the United Arab Emirates, Russia and Europe are also investing into new missions and independent systems. Space has emerged as a strategic arena in the global struggle for power, with competition for influence and dominance extending far beyond nation states. Private companies control an ever-growing share of space infrastructure, led by Elon Musk's SpaceX and its Starlink satellite network. The war in Ukraine offers a stark illustration of the geopolitical leverage that control over space infrastructure can provide. Since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, Starlink has become a central part of Ukraine's communications and defense. The coordination of military operations now depends, in part, on decisions made not by governments, but by a private company. Control of infrastructure in orbit translates into influence on Earth. At the same time, efforts to safeguard these critical systems are adding further momentum to the militarisation of space.
While space technology is advancing at unprecedented speed, the rules governing it belong to a very different era. The 1967 Outer Space Treaty, adopted under the auspices of the United Nations, laid the foundation for international space law. It prohibits national claims of sovereignty over celestial bodies and the placement of weapons of mass destruction in orbit, but leaves many questions unresolved. Nearly six decades later, nations have yet to agree on a comprehensive framework of rules for this new space age.
The film takes viewers into a race that is already underway: a global struggle between nations, militaries and corporations for control of critical infrastructure, geopolitical influence and the rules that will shape our future in space — a place we're all increasingly dependent upon.
